For a 50-person Indian company, I’d shortlist these three based on the current published commercial terms. There isn’t enough public pricing to honestly calculate one “cheapest” annual cost, so the purchase decision should be based on the all-in quote you negotiate.

Option	Value proposition	Exact trade-off	Verify before paying
Cleartrip OOO	₹0 subscription / no extra platform charges publicly advertised; GST-compliant. 
OOO
	More self-serve than a traditional TMC.	Written confirmation that there are no transaction/service fees; cancellation/reissue charges; dedicated RM; 24×7 SLA; credit terms.
MMT myBiz	Corporate platform with negotiated service fee.	1.5% payment-gateway fee on wallet/card repayments, on top of agreed service fee. 
MakeMyTrip
	Per-booking fee, payment method, cancellation/reissue charges, credit limit, support SLA.
Thomas Cook India	More fully managed: air, hotels, rail, visa, forex, MICE, dedicated servicing and 24×7 emergency desk. 
Thomas Cook
	Likely higher service cost; pricing is quote-based.	Management/transaction fees, implant cost, after-hours charges, SLA, credit period and refund handling.
Purchase-ready RFQ

Ask each for a 12-month all-in quote using the same assumptions: 50 travellers, expected annual travel spend, domestic/international split and ~number of trips.

My shortlist order for evaluation: Cleartrip OOO → MMT myBiz → Thomas Cook, not as a quality ranking, but because it lets you compare a low-fee platform against increasingly managed-service models.

Do not sign until cancellation/reissue fees, GST, payment fees, refund timelines, 24×7 response SLA and termination terms are explicitly written into the commercial agreement.
